gen-dafont-neuropolitical-gf-kadwa: Glowing tube letters, drifting apart one by one. Neuropolitical lights up the top, and Kadwa, a text serif with open-ended curves and a large x-height, grounds the lines beneath it.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-inter: Neon-tube letters, spaced apart and glowing: that's Neuropolitical. Inter, with big counters in a tall lowercase, handles the steady reading, while the heading is at its best glowing in display.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-mulish: Glowing neon letters, pulled apart: that is Neuropolitical. Mulish, with a large x-height, short ascenders and horseshoe-open apertures, holds up nicely at fairly modest sizes without any stroke contrast.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-roboto-slab: Neuropolitical spaces its single-nib neon-tube letters well apart. It is best at glowing display work, while Roboto Slab, a slab-serif with open throats, handles the structured reading through a dominant middle zone.
gen-dafont-neuropolitical-rubik: Strokes shaped like neon glass tubing give Neuropolitical its glow. Rubik, with big lowercase and round letters clear at small sizes, does the quiet text work the heading is too showy for.
gen-dafont-nordic-bitter: Brush-dab spacing and one cut width everywhere: that is Nordic, a heading with cramped openings and ancient weight. Bitter, a slab-serif, has an open lowercase you can see right through.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-epunda-slab: Epunda Slab, a serif with tall rounded forms and a visibly gaping c. Nordic, the heading, is closed and cramped in one width, which makes that openness the best thing about the pair.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-fauna-one: Nordic cuts every stroke to one width, closed up tight and sparingly spaced. Fauna One, with a tall middle band and a generous entry into the e, stays open where the heading stays shut.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-hanuman: Every stroke in Nordic is cut to a single width, with cramped, closed shapes. Hanuman, a refined serif with a high-waisted lowercase and wide-set terminals on s, opens everything back up.
gen-dafont-nordic-gf-piazzolla: Piazzolla, a serif whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals and whose e opens like a pried clasp, has real authority. Nordic, flat and closed, hands off to text that flows smoothly.
